thesis: One architecture family, measured from the smallest member to the largest.

members.name: DeepSeek-V2
members.note: The first MLA + DeepSeekMoE generation: 160 routed experts, top-6, two shared experts, 60 layers.

members.name: DeepSeek-V2-Lite
members.note: The only member small enough to instrument on one free GPU. Same MLA + DeepSeekMoE grammar as every model after it.

members.name: DeepSeek-V3
members.note: The model that fixed the family's silhouette: 256 routed experts, one shared expert, 8 active, MLA throughout.

members.name: DeepSeek-V3.1
members.note: Same weights architecture as V3, retrained for hybrid thinking. Included to show that a generation can change behaviour without changing shape.

members.name: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp
members.note: DeepSeek Sparse Attention: a 64-head index selects 2,048 keys per query, so attention stops paying for the whole context.

members.name: DeepSeek-R1
members.note: Reasoning post-training on the V3 base: the same 61-layer MLA + 256-expert MoE, with RL-shaped behaviour rather than a new shape.

members.name: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
members.note: The first family member with hash-routed MoE layers and a hybrid compressed/sparse attention stack; 1M context at 13B active.

members.name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
members.note: The 1.6T flagship: 384 experts, 61 layers, 49B active — the same sparsity ratio as V3 at 2.4× the width.

members.name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
members.note: Causal encoder–decoder: 8B active on the input path, 16B on the output path, three MTP heads, and KV shared across layers.

generations.label: R1 · 2025
generations.change: reasoning RL on V3; shape unchanged

generations.label: V4 · 2026
generations.change: CSA/HCA, hash routing, FP4 experts, 1M context

generations.label: V4.1 · 2026
generations.change: Causal encoder–decoder, shared KV across layers, multimodal
